column1: # The level ladder for core-es — the controlled vocabulary for the `level`
# column of every other source file, and the order those levels climb in.
# Columns: id
# **The order of the rows is the ladder.** Level is a *ceiling* everywhere in the
# app — `a2` means "a2 and below" — and that comparison used to be
# `CEFR_LEVELS.indexOf(...)` against a closed enum in `src/domain/content/model.ts`.
# Chinese is taught in HSK bands and Japanese in JLPT ones, so an enum of six CEFR
# codes is a Spanish fact in a model every pack shares; see
# docs/tasks/language-matrix.md §7, where this is the schema decision it calls
# the most urgent. The build now emits this order into the manifest and every
# ordering read comes from there.
# The build fails on a level used in a source file but missing here, which is the
# same guard `topics.tsv` gives its own column. It does **not** fail on a
# declared level nothing uses: the ladder is the curriculum's shape and may be
# declared ahead of the rows that fill it — only the levels actually present are
# advertised in the manifest.
# `label` is optional and is left off here on purpose. A CEFR code reads correctly
# as its own name once upper-cased, which is what the app falls back to, and a
# label repeating `A1` would be a second place for it to go stale. A pack whose
# ladder is not self-naming declares one: `hsk1
# Do not reorder these rows. The ladder is the order, so moving one changes what
# every `?level=` link and every course scope means.
a1
a2
b1
b2
c1
c2
